previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia s/p cord blood transplant, chronic GVHD, steroid-induced diabetes, and dilated cardiomyopathy, was admitted for a persistent cough of one week’s duration. He had mild fatigue and increased oxygen use at rest but no fever or dyspnea. Initial chest X-ray showed no acute process. CT chest revealed new bronchial wall thickening, mucus plugging, and ground-glass opacities, more consistent with infection than GVHD flare. Respiratory viral panel and blood cultures were negative. He was treated with levofloxacin and continued on home immunosuppressants without steroid escalation. IVIG was administered as part of his scheduled therapy. His symptoms improved, oxygen requirements decreased, and he was discharged home with a short course of oral antibiotics and allopurinol for elevated uric acid. Follow-up was arranged with oncology and a new primary care provider.
problems: Acute upper respiratory infections of unspecified site
Secondary diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, not stated as uncontrolled, or unspecified

Brief Hospital Course:
___ is a ___ male with a history of AML s/p allo cord SCT in 
___ complicated by ARDS/?BOOP with a prolonged ICU course, 
chronic GVHD, and prednisone induced DM who notes chills and a 
cough since this morning with fevers, admitted for workup of 
fever. 
.
1. Fever, malaise:  Patient relayed a history of fever to 102 
several days prior to presentation accompanied by general 
malaise, yet these symptoms were not relayed to the covering 
oncologist until he presented in routine follow-up to the 
___ clinic on ___.  He remained afebrile throughout his 
short hospital course, and his malaise and nausea subsided.  
Chest XR showed no acute pneumonia.  Blood cultures were 
obtained which were negative at the time of discharge.  Stool 
culture were sent due to history of diarrhea x 1, and were 
pending at the time of discharge. He showed a lymphocytosis in 
his differential cell count, possibly suggesting viral 
infection.  He improved overnight and was discharged in the 
afternoon of ___ with strict instructions to call the 
covering oncologist right away in response to febrile symptoms. 
He was started on ciprofloxacin on the night of admission for a 
possible enteric infection, and was discharged on an additional 
5 day course.  Voriconazole was discontinued due to a QTc 
prolongation interaction with cipro.
.
2. AML s/p allogeneic cord stem cell transplant day>500: The 
patient was continued on cellcept, viral prophylaxis with 
acyclovir, PCP prophylaxis with bactrim.  His cell counts were 
stable with an ANC>1000. 
.
3. Graft versus host disease:  this has typically manifested in 
the joints and skin.  He was continued on prednisone with 
bactrim for PCP prophylaxis and felt no significant joint pains 
while hospitalized.
.
4. Aspergillus sinusitis: voriconazole was stopped due to an 
interaction with cipro as noted above.
.
5. BOOP/COP:  breathing status at his baseline, requiring ___ 
NC at first and titrated down to RA.
